Header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Time: 09:30 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Catalyst Tech CTO), Jordan Lee (Lead ML Eng), Tara Singh (Eng Manager)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics (streaming, model params, retry behaviour). Customer interested in low-latency responses for an in-app assistant, curious about cost tradeoffs and security (KMS, retention). Agreed to benchmark and schedule infra deep dive.

Topics: streaming responses, temperature/top_p, max_tokens and cost, retries/backoff/idempotency, SDK examples, Console observability, Optimize recommendations (batching, cache, quantization suggestions)

[00:00] Michael Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um Alicia, Jordan, Tara, good to meet you all. I'm Michael, I'll run the demo and Priya will cover the technical bits, Samir on standby for questions.
[00:15] Alicia Gomez: Thanks, yeah excited to see how Redwood's hosted API can help our in-app assistant, we're most worried about latency and cost, and also certs--like enterprise security.
[00:27] Priya Rao: Cool. Quick agenda, we'll show the API flow (curl + SDK), live streaming example, tuning params, retry semantics, and then the Console + Optimize tips. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Awesome, we have a guesstimate of about 15k requests/day, average 50 tokens per response, but spikes during mornings. Also we use GCP mostly, but we need data residency in us-east for now.
[00:57] Priya Rao: Noted. Hosted API can route to region and we have model variants with different latency/cost profiles. We'll show streaming which helps perceived latency for your UI.

[02:10] Demo start - API basics
[02:12] Michael Chen: Here's the curl example (reads): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"stream":true}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/generate  -- this will stream chunked responses.
[02:35] Tara Singh: When you say stream true, is that server-sent events or a websocket?
[02:40] Priya Rao: It's chunked HTTP streaming - SSE-like chunks so the browser can append tokens as they come. It reduces time-to-first-token signficantly. Note: in some SDKs we also have a websockets client for high-throughput.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: Any gotchas with reconnects? If a stream drops mid-response do we need to re-send whole prompt?
[03:12] Priya Rao: Good question. We recommend idempotency via request IDs, and clients can resume by sending the last known message id; for short interruptions we typically fall back to a retry with exponential backoff. We also expose a "delta" streaming format in the SDK to handle partial apply.

[05:00] Parameters and cost tradeoffs
[05:02] Michael Chen: On model params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and response_format. Temperature controls randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling. Lower temperature, lower variance — usually cheaper indirectly because fewer tokens for clarifications, but main cost is per-token generation.
[05:30] Michael Chen: Max_tokens sets upper bound; important for cost cap. Also we have stop sequences and token budgets on the route level.
[05:48] Jordan Lee: Do you support token-level billing and estimates per request?
[05:54] Priya Rao: Yes we provide estimated tokens in response headers and Console shows per-route token breakdowns and cost. You can set quotas and rate limits as well.

[07:20] Retries, idempotency and error handling
[07:22] Priya Rao: Retry behaviour: client should use idempotency keys for non-streaming ops. For streaming we advise detecting connection errors and either resume or replay depending on state. Exponential backoff + jitter is recommended. We also return consistent error codes (429 rate limit, 503 transient).
[07:48] Tara Singh: If we hit 429 a lot during spikes what's the best strategy?
[07:52] Priya Rao: Two approaches: burst protection via Dedicated or reserved capacity, or graceful degradation: shorter responses, cache common prefixes, prewarm for peak windows. Optimize module can suggest batching/caching config based on your workload.

[09:10] Console and observability
[09:12] Michael Chen: Quick tour of Console - route dashboards show latency percentiles, token usage, per-model breakdown, and traces for slow requests. You can filter by API key or user id to troubleshoot.
[09:30] Alicia Gomez: Can the Console export audit logs to our SIEM? We need searchable logs for SOC2.
[09:36] Samir Patel: Yes, we integrate with SIEM via S3/GC storage and have audit events for request metadata. We also support customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest and envelope encryption.

[11:05] Onboarding and security questions
[11:07] Alicia Gomez: On data retention, we need 90-day retention with logs, and option to not store raw user content.
[11:13] Michael Chen: We support configurable retention policies per account and a no-persist mode where we don't persist customer payloads. For Private customers we offer on-prem package.
[11:25] Jordan Lee: KMS integration - how would that work if we use GCP KMS?
[11:30] Priya Rao: We have KMS integrations across AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options. For hosted, you can bring your own key and we handle envelope encryption; for Private, keys stay in your environment.

[13:00] Live streaming demo (live chat in demo app)
[13:05] Priya Rao: I'll send a streaming request now, you'll see partial tokens arrive. (typing noises)
[13:22] [stream chunks] Speaker (demo): "Hello, how can I help you today..."
[13:40] Tara Singh: That's pretty smooth. What's your p99?
[13:45] Priya Rao: For the redwood-1.1 family in us-east, p50 ~ 90ms token, p95 ~ 220ms for conversational size of ~256 tokens. We tune kernels based on sequence length and use KV cache and prefix caching to speed up repeated contexts.

[15:30] Optimize recommendations
[15:32] Michael Chen: The Optimize tool will analyze logs and suggest batching sizes, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles that are compatible with your accuracy budget. For example, quantize to int8 for cheaper inference if your eval set shows <1% quality delta.
[15:55] Jordan Lee: Do you provide the eval harness or do we bring our own prompt set?
[16:00] Priya Rao: You can bring a prompt set; we also provide eval harness templates. We'll run regression alerts against your golden prompts and notify if quality drops after a model change or quantization.

[18:10] Pricing and capacity
[18:12] Michael Chen: Hosted pricing is usage-based; we have per-token rates and discounted tiers for committed volume. For consistent high TPS you can reserve capacity in Dedicated. We'll send a sample pricing sheet after the call.
[18:30] Alicia Gomez: We're very cost-sensitive, our execs will want clear TCO for 6-12 months.
[18:35] Michael Chen: Understood, we'll put together a TCO comparison (OpenAI vs Redwood hosted vs Dedicated) with latency and unit-cost numbers.

[20:00] Technical deep dive requests
[20:05] Jordan Lee: We'd like a deeper session on autoscaling and exact retry semantics and how the KV cache works with multi-tenant workloads. Also want to validate latency with our prompt set.
[20:18] Priya Rao: We'll schedule a SE-led deep dive. Priya + Samir will join; please invite your infra folks. We'll also propose a short benchmark plan.

[22:30] Common objections and clarifications
[22:32] Tara Singh: Concern - vendor lock in. If we start with hosted, can we move to Private later?
[22:40] Michael Chen: Yes, we support migrations. Same API surface and model catalog across hosted, Dedicated and Private—your prompts and routes can be ported. Some infra configuration differs but we provide migration guides.
[22:55] Alicia Gomez: Any known limitations on content moderation or PII detection?
[23:00] Samir Patel: We have built-in classification pipelines and can add custom filters in the request pipeline. For sensitive data we recommend no-persist + on-prem if compliance requires it.

[25:00] Recap and next steps
[25:02] Michael Chen: Quick recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2/security docs, Priya to share benchmark plan, and we'll schedule a deep dive for autoscale and KV cache. Customer to share prompt set and success criteria.
[25:20] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good. One more: can you show an example SDK call with automatic retries?
[25:26] Priya Rao: Yep, in Node SDK it looks like: client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-1.1', messages: [...], max_tokens: 200, retry: {retries: 3, factor: 2, minTimeout: 200}}) - SDK has built-in backoff and idempotency helpers.

[27:10] Closeout
[27:12] Jordan Lee: Thanks, that was helpful. We'll sync internally and send prompts.
[27:18] Tara Singh: Thanks Michael and team.
[27:20] Michael Chen: Thank you all, we'll follow up with the items in chat.

(Transcript trims remaining chatter and wrap-up.)
